questions.text: Let $\alpha, \alpha+2, \alpha \in \mathbb{Z}$, be the roots of the quadratic equation $$x(x+2)+(x+1)(x+3)+(x+2)(x+4)+\ldots+(x+n-1)(x+n+1)=4n \quad \text{for some } n \in \mathbb{N}.$$ Then $n+\alpha$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
The LHS is $\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(x+k)(x+k+2) = nx^2 + n(n+1)x + \dfrac{(n-1)n(2n-1)}{6} + n(n-1)$.
Dividing by $n$: $x^2+(n+1)x+\dfrac{(n-1)(2n-1)}{6}+n-5=0$.
Roots differ by $2$, so discriminant $=4$: $(n+1)^2-\dfrac{2(2n^2-3n+1)}{3}-4n+20=4$.
This simplifies to $n^2=49$, so $n=7$.
Sum of roots $2\alpha+2=-(n+1)=-8 \Rightarrow \alpha=-5$.
Hence $n+\alpha=2$.

questions.text: Let $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{R}$ be such that the system of linear equations $$\begin{aligned} x+2y+z&=5\\ 2x+y+\alpha z&=5\\ 8x+4y+\beta z&=18 \end{aligned}$$ has no solution. Then $\dfrac{\beta}{\alpha}$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
For no solution, $\Delta=\begin{vmatrix}1&2&1\\2&1&\alpha\\8&4&\beta\end{vmatrix}=12\alpha-3\beta=0$, so $\beta=4\alpha$.
Then the third equation's LHS is $4\times$ the second's: $8x+4y+4\alpha z$, but $4\times5=20\neq18$, so the system is inconsistent.
Hence $\dfrac{\beta}{\alpha}=4$.

questions.text:
Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\1&\alpha\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}3&3\\\beta&2\end{bmatrix}$. If $A^2-4A+I=O$ and $B^2-5B-6I=O$, then among the two statements :
$(\text{S1}): \left[(B-A)(B+A)\right]^T=\begin{bmatrix}13&15\\7&10\end{bmatrix}$
and
$(\text{S2}): \det\left(\operatorname{adj}(A+B)\right)=-5$,
questions.sol:
By Cayley–Hamilton, $A^2-(\operatorname{tr}A)A+(\det A)I=O$, so $\operatorname{tr}A=1+\alpha=4 \Rightarrow \alpha=3$ (and $\det A=1$ ✓).
For $B$: $\det B=6-3\beta=-6 \Rightarrow \beta=4$.
$B-A=\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\3&-1\end{bmatrix}$, $B+A=\begin{bmatrix}4&5\\5&5\end{bmatrix}$, product $=\begin{bmatrix}13&15\\7&10\end{bmatrix}$; its transpose is $\begin{bmatrix}13&7\\15&10\end{bmatrix}$, so (S1) is wrong.
$\det(A+B)=20-25=-5$ and for $2\times2$, $\det(\operatorname{adj}M)=\det M=-5$, so (S2) is correct.

questions.text: Let $A$ be the set of first $101$ terms of an A.P., whose first term is $1$ and the common difference is $5$ and let $B$ be the set of first $71$ terms of an A.P., whose first term is $9$ and the common difference is $7$. Then the number of elements in $A \cap B$, which are divisible by $3$, is :
questions.sol:
$A=\{1,6,\ldots,501\}$ ($x\equiv1 \pmod 5$), $B=\{9,16,\ldots,499\}$ ($x\equiv2 \pmod 7$).
Common terms: $x\equiv16 \pmod{35}$, i.e. $x=16+35t \le 499 \Rightarrow t=0,1,\ldots,13$.
$16+35t\equiv 1+2t \equiv 0 \pmod 3 \Rightarrow t\equiv1 \pmod 3$: $t=1,4,7,10,13$.
So $5$ elements.

questions.text: The number of seven-digit numbers, that can be formed by using the digits $1, 2, 3, 5$ and $7$ such that each digit is used at least once, is :
questions.sol:
Five distinct digits fill seven places, so the extra two places give pattern $(3,1,1,1,1)$ or $(2,2,1,1,1)$.
Pattern $(3,1,1,1,1)$: $5\cdot\dfrac{7!}{3!}=4200$.
Pattern $(2,2,1,1,1)$: $\binom{5}{2}\cdot\dfrac{7!}{2!\,2!}=12600$.
Total $=16800$.

questions.text: Let the mid points of the sides of a triangle $ABC$ be $\left(\dfrac{5}{2},7\right), \left(\dfrac{5}{2},3\right)$ and $(4,5)$. If its incentre is $(h,k)$, then $3h+k$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
With midpoints $D\left(\tfrac52,7\right), E\left(\tfrac52,3\right), F(4,5)$, the vertices are $E+F-D=(4,1)$, $D+F-E=(4,9)$, $D+E-F=(1,5)$.
Take $A(4,1), B(4,9), C(1,5)$: $a=BC=5$, $b=CA=5$, $c=AB=8$.
$h=\dfrac{5\cdot4+5\cdot4+8\cdot1}{18}=\dfrac{8}{3}$, $k=\dfrac{5\cdot1+5\cdot9+8\cdot5}{18}=5$.
$3h+k=8+5=13$.

questions.text: Let an ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$, $a<b$, pass through the point $(4,3)$ and have eccentricity $\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{3}$. Then the length of its latus rectum is :
questions.sol:
Since $aThrough $(4,3)$: $\dfrac{16\cdot9}{4b^2}+\dfrac{9}{b^2}=\dfrac{45}{b^2}=1 \Rightarrow b^2=45,\ a^2=20$.
Latus rectum $=\dfrac{2a^2}{b}=\dfrac{40}{3\sqrt5}=\dfrac{8\sqrt5}{3}$.

questions.text: If $\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{18}\right)\sin\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{18}\right)\sin\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{18}\right)=K$, then the value of $\sin\left(\dfrac{10K\pi}{3}\right)$ is :
questions.sol:
$K=\sin10^\circ\sin50^\circ\sin70^\circ=\sin10^\circ\sin(60^\circ-10^\circ)\sin(60^\circ+10^\circ)=\dfrac{\sin30^\circ}{4}=\dfrac18$.
$\dfrac{10K\pi}{3}=\dfrac{10\pi}{24}=\dfrac{5\pi}{12}$.
$\sin75^\circ=\dfrac{\sqrt3+1}{2\sqrt2}$.

questions.text: Let $S=\{x \in [-\pi,\pi] : \sin x\,(\sin x+\cos x)=a,\ a \in \mathbb{Z}\}$. Then $n(S)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$\sin x(\sin x+\cos x)=\dfrac12+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\sin\left(2x-\dfrac\pi4\right)\in\left[\dfrac{1-\sqrt2}{2},\dfrac{1+\sqrt2}{2}\right]$, so $a\in\{0,1\}$.
$a=0$: $\sin x=0 \Rightarrow x=-\pi,0,\pi$; or $\tan x=-1 \Rightarrow x=-\dfrac\pi4,\dfrac{3\pi}4$: $5$ solutions.
$a=1$: $\sin x\cos x=\cos^2x \Rightarrow \cos x=0$ ($x=\pm\dfrac\pi2$) or $\tan x=1$ ($x=\dfrac\pi4,-\dfrac{3\pi}4$): $4$ solutions.
$n(S)=9$.

questions.text: If the point of intersection of the lines $\dfrac{x+1}{3}=\dfrac{y+a}{5}=\dfrac{z+b+1}{7}$ and $\dfrac{x-2}{1}=\dfrac{y-b}{4}=\dfrac{z-2a}{7}$ lies on $xy$-plane, then the value of $a+b$ is :
questions.sol:
Points: $(3t-1,\,5t-a,\,7t-b-1)$ and $(s+2,\,4s+b,\,7s+2a)$.
$z=0$: $t=\dfrac{b+1}{7}$, $s=-\dfrac{2a}{7}$.
Equal $x$: $3(b+1)-7=-2a+14 \Rightarrow 2a+3b=18$.
Equal $y$: $5(b+1)-7a=-8a+7b \Rightarrow a=2b-5$.
So $b=4,\ a=3$ and $a+b=7$.

questions.text: If $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are two vectors such that $|\vec{a}|=2$ and $|\vec{b}|=3$, then the maximum value of $3\left|\left(3\vec{a}+2\vec{b}\right)\right|+4\left|\left(3\vec{a}-2\vec{b}\right)\right|$ is :
questions.sol:
Let $u=|3\vec a+2\vec b|$, $v=|3\vec a-2\vec b|$. Then $u^2+v^2=2(9|\vec a|^2+4|\vec b|^2)=144$.
By Cauchy–Schwarz, $3u+4v\le\sqrt{3^2+4^2}\sqrt{u^2+v^2}=5\cdot12=60$.
Equality at $u=7.2,\ v=9.6$, i.e. $u^2-v^2=24\,\vec a\cdot\vec b=-40.32$, $\vec a\cdot\vec b=-1.68\in[-6,6]$, so attainable.
Maximum $=60$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let a line $L$ passing through the point $(1,1,1)$ be perpendicular to both the vectors $2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$. If $P(a,b,c)$ is the foot of perpendicular from the origin on the line $L$, then the value of $34(a+b+c)$ is :
questions.sol:
Direction of $L$: $(2,2,1)\times(1,2,2)=(2,-3,2)$.
General point $P=(1+2t,\,1-3t,\,1+2t)$.
$\overrightarrow{OP}\perp L$: $2(1+2t)-3(1-3t)+2(1+2t)=1+17t=0 \Rightarrow t=-\dfrac1{17}$.
$P=\left(\dfrac{15}{17},\dfrac{20}{17},\dfrac{15}{17}\right)$, so $34(a+b+c)=34\cdot\dfrac{50}{17}=100$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to2}\frac{\sin\left(x^3-5x^2+ax+b\right)}{\left(\sqrt{x-1}-1\right)\log_e(x-1)}=m$, then $a+b+m$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
As $x\to2$: $\sqrt{x-1}-1\sim\dfrac{x-2}{2}$ and $\log_e(x-1)\sim x-2$, so the denominator $\sim\dfrac{(x-2)^2}{2}$.
For a finite limit, $p(x)=x^3-5x^2+ax+b$ must have a double root at $2$: $p(2)=2a+b-12=0$, $p'(2)=a-8=0$.
So $a=8,\ b=-4$ and $p(x)=(x-2)^2(x-1)$.
$m=\lim\dfrac{(x-2)^2(x-1)}{(x-2)^2/2}=2$.
$a+b+m=8-4+2=6$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If the curve $y=f(x)$ passes through the point $(1,e)$ and satisfies the differential equation $dy=y\left(2+\log_e x\right)dx,\ x>0$, then $f(e)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{dy}{y}=(2+\log_e x)\,dx \Rightarrow \log_e y=2x+x\log_e x-x+C=x+x\log_e x+C$.
At $(1,e)$: $1=1+0+C \Rightarrow C=0$.
At $x=e$: $\log_e y=e+e=2e$, so $f(e)=e^{2e}$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The number of critical points of the function $f(x)=\begin{cases}\left|\dfrac{\sin x}{x}\right|, & x\neq0\\ 1, & x=0\end{cases}$ in the interval $(-2\pi,2\pi)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$g(x)=\dfrac{\sin x}{x}$ (with $g(0)=1$) is smooth and even, and $f=|g|$.
$x=0$: $f'(0)=0$ (local maximum) — one critical point.
$x=\pm\pi$: $g=0$ changes sign, $f$ is not differentiable — two critical points.
In $(\pi,2\pi)$, $g'(x)=0 \iff \tan x=x$ has exactly one root ($x\approx4.49$), and by symmetry one in $(-2\pi,-\pi)$; none in $(0,\pi)$.
Total $=5$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $[\cdot]$ denote the greatest integer function. Then the value of $\displaystyle\int_0^3\left(\frac{e^x+e^{-x}}{[x]!}\right)dx$ is :
questions.sol:
Let $F(x)=e^x-e^{-x}$, an antiderivative of $e^x+e^{-x}$; $F(0)=0$.
Integral $=\dfrac{F(1)-F(0)}{0!}+\dfrac{F(2)-F(1)}{1!}+\dfrac{F(3)-F(2)}{2!}$.
$=F(2)+\dfrac{F(3)-F(2)}{2}=\dfrac{F(2)+F(3)}{2}$.
$=\dfrac12\left(e^2+e^3-\dfrac1{e^2}-\dfrac1{e^3}\right)$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution curve of the differential equation $(1+\sin x)\dfrac{dy}{dx}+(y+1)\cos x=0,\ y(0)=0$. If the curve $y=y(x)$ passes through the point $\left(\alpha,\dfrac{-1}{2}\right)$, then a value of $\alpha$ is :
questions.sol:
The equation is $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[(1+\sin x)(y+1)\right]=0$, so $(1+\sin x)(y+1)=C$.
$y(0)=0 \Rightarrow C=1$.
At $y=-\dfrac12$: $(1+\sin\alpha)\cdot\dfrac12=1 \Rightarrow \sin\alpha=1$.
So $\alpha=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If the domain of the function $f(x)=\sqrt{\log_{(0.6)}\left(\left|\dfrac{2x-5}{x^2-4}\right|\right)}$ is $(-\infty,a]\cup\{b\}\cup[c,d)\cup(e,\infty)$, then the value of $a+b+c+d+e$ is __________.
questions.sol:
Need $0<\left|\dfrac{2x-5}{x^2-4}\right|\le1$, with $x\neq\pm2$, $x\neq\dfrac52$.
$(2x-5)^2\le(x^2-4)^2 \iff (x^2-2x+1)(x^2+2x-9)\ge0 \iff (x-1)^2(x^2+2x-9)\ge0$.
So $x\le-1-\sqrt{10}$, or $x=1$, or $x\ge-1+\sqrt{10}$ (and $\pm2$ are not in these sets).
Removing $x=\dfrac52$: domain $=(-\infty,-1-\sqrt{10}]\cup\{1\}\cup\left[-1+\sqrt{10},\dfrac52\right)\cup\left(\dfrac52,\infty\right)$.
$a+b+c+d+e=-2+1+\dfrac52+\dfrac52=4$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $a, b, c \in \{1,2,3,4\}$. If the probability, that $ax^2+2\sqrt{2}\,bx+c>0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$, is $\dfrac{m}{n}$, $\gcd(m,n)=1$, then $m+n$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Since $a>0$, we need discriminant $8b^2-4ac<0$, i.e. $ac>2b^2$. Total choices $4^3=64$.
$b=1$: $ac>2$; of the 16 pairs only $(1,1),(1,2),(2,1)$ fail, so $13$.
$b=2$: $ac>8$: $(3,3),(3,4),(4,3),(4,4)$, so $4$.
$b=3,4$: $ac>18$ impossible.
Probability $=\dfrac{17}{64}$, so $m+n=81$.

questions.text: Let a circle $C$ have its centre in the first quadrant, intersect the coordinate axes at exactly three points and cut off equal intercepts from the coordinate axes. If the length of the chord of $C$ on the line $x+y=1$ is $\sqrt{14}$, then the square of the radius of $C$ is __________.
questions.sol:
Equal intercepts give centre $(h,h)$, $h>0$; meeting the axes at exactly three points means the circle passes through the origin, so $r^2=2h^2$.
Distance from centre to $x+y=1$: $d=\dfrac{|2h-1|}{\sqrt2}$.
Half chord: $r^2-d^2=\dfrac{14}{4}$, so $2h^2-\dfrac{(2h-1)^2}{2}=\dfrac72 \Rightarrow 4h-1=7 \Rightarrow h=2$.
$r^2=8$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If $\alpha=\displaystyle\int_0^{2\sqrt{3}}\log_2\left(x^2+4\right)dx+\int_2^4\sqrt{2^x-4}\,dx$, then $\alpha^2$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Let $g(x)=\log_2(x^2+4)$ on $[0,2\sqrt3]$; it increases from $g(0)=2$ to $g(2\sqrt3)=4$.
Its inverse is $g^{-1}(y)=\sqrt{2^y-4}$ on $[2,4]$.
$\displaystyle\int_0^{2\sqrt3}g+\int_2^4g^{-1}=2\sqrt3\cdot4-0\cdot2=8\sqrt3$.
$\alpha^2=192$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The dimensional formula of $\dfrac{1}{2}\epsilon_o E^2$ ($\epsilon_o$ = permittivity of vacuum and E = electric field) is $\mathrm{M^aL^bT^c}$. The value of $2a-b+c=$ ________.
questions.sol: $\tfrac{1}{2}\epsilon_o E^2$ is energy per unit volume. $[\text{energy density}] = \dfrac{\mathrm{ML^2T^{-2}}}{\mathrm{L^3}} = \mathrm{M^1L^{-1}T^{-2}}$. So $a=1,\ b=-1,\ c=-2$ and $2a-b+c = 2+1-2 = 1$.

questions.text:
The diameter of a wire measured by a screw gauge of least count 0.001 cm is 0.08 cm. The length measured by a scale of least count 0.1 cm is 150 cm. When a weight of 100 N is applied to the wire, the extension in length is 0.5 cm, measured by a micrometer of least count 0.001 cm. The error in the measured Young's modulus is $\alpha\times10^9\ \mathrm{N/m^2}$. The value of $\alpha$ is ________.
(Ignore the contribution of the load to Young's modulus error calculation)
questions.sol:
$Y = \dfrac{4FL}{\pi d^2\,\Delta L} = \dfrac{4(100)(1.5)}{\pi(8\times10^{-4})^2(5\times10^{-3})} \approx 5.97\times10^{10}\ \mathrm{N/m^2}$.
$\dfrac{\Delta Y}{Y} = 2\dfrac{\Delta d}{d} + \dfrac{\Delta L}{L} + \dfrac{\Delta(\Delta L)}{\Delta L} = 2\cdot\dfrac{0.001}{0.08} + \dfrac{0.1}{150} + \dfrac{0.001}{0.5} \approx 0.0277$.
$\Delta Y \approx 5.97\times10^{10}\times0.0277 \approx 1.65\times10^9\ \mathrm{N/m^2}$, so $\alpha = 1.65$.

questions.text: The velocity of a particle is given as $\vec{v} = -x\hat{i} + 2y\hat{j} - z\hat{k}$ m/s. The magnitude of acceleration at point (1, 2, 4) is ________ $\mathrm{m/s^2}$.
questions.sol:
$v_x=-x,\ v_y=2y,\ v_z=-z$. Then $a_x = \dfrac{dv_x}{dt} = -v_x = x$, $a_y = 2v_y = 4y$, $a_z = -v_z = z$.
At $(1,2,4)$: $\vec{a} = \hat{i} + 8\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$, so $|\vec{a}| = \sqrt{1+64+16} = 9\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The position of an object having mass 0.1 kg as a function of time $t$ is given as $\vec{r} = \left(10t^2\hat{i} + 5t^3\hat{j}\right)$ m. At $t = 1$ s, which of the following statements are correct ?
A. The linear momentum $\vec{p} = \left(2\hat{i} + 1.5\hat{j}\right)$ kg-m/s.
B. The force acting on the object $\vec{F} = \left(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}\right)$N.
C. The angular momentum of the object about its origin $\vec{L} = 15\ \hat{k}$ J s.
D. The torque acting on the object about its origin $\vec{\tau} = 20\ \hat{k}$ N m.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
At $t=1$: $\vec{r} = 10\hat{i}+5\hat{j}$, $\vec{v} = 20t\hat{i}+15t^2\hat{j} = 20\hat{i}+15\hat{j}$, $\vec{a} = 20\hat{i}+30t\hat{j} = 20\hat{i}+30\hat{j}$.
$\vec{p} = m\vec{v} = 2\hat{i}+1.5\hat{j}$ (A true); $\vec{F} = m\vec{a} = 2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}$ (B true).
$\vec{L} = \vec{r}\times\vec{p} = (10)(1.5)-(5)(2) = 5\hat{k}$ (C false).
$\vec{\tau} = \vec{r}\times\vec{F} = (10)(3)-(5)(2) = 20\hat{k}$ (D true). Hence A, B and D only.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A planet ($\mathrm{P_1}$) is moving around the star of mass $2M$ in the orbit of radius $R$. Another planet ($\mathrm{P_2}$) is moving around another star of mass $4M$ in a orbit of radius $2R$. Ratio of time periods of revolution of $\mathrm{P_2}$ and $\mathrm{P_1}$ is ________.
questions.sol:
$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{r^3}{GM_s}}$, so $T \propto \sqrt{r^3/M_s}$.
$\dfrac{T_2}{T_1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{(2R)^3/(4M)}{R^3/(2M)}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{8}{2}} = 2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A particle is rotating in a circular path and at any instant its motion can be described as $\theta = \dfrac{5t^4}{40} - \dfrac{t^3}{3}$. The angular acceleration of the particle after 10 seconds is ________ $\mathrm{rad/s^2}$.
questions.sol:
$\omega = \dfrac{d\theta}{dt} = \dfrac{t^3}{2} - t^2$.
$\alpha = \dfrac{d\omega}{dt} = \dfrac{3t^2}{2} - 2t$.
At $t=10$ s: $\alpha = 150 - 20 = 130\ \mathrm{rad/s^2}$.

questions.text: A parallel plate air capacitor has a capacitance C. When it is half filled as show in figure with a dielectric constant $K = 5$, the percentage increase in the capacitance is ________.
questions.sol:
The two layers (each of thickness $d/2$) are in series, with $C = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{d}$.
Dielectric layer: $C_1 = \dfrac{K\epsilon_0 A}{d/2} = 10C$; air layer: $C_2 = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{d/2} = 2C$.
$C' = \dfrac{C_1C_2}{C_1+C_2} = \dfrac{20C^2}{12C} = \dfrac{5}{3}C$.
Increase $= \dfrac{2}{3}\times100\% \approx 66.67\%$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Heat is supplied to a diatomic gas at constant pressure. Then the ratio of $\Delta Q : \Delta U : \Delta W$ is ______.
questions.sol:
For a diatomic gas $C_V = \tfrac{5}{2}R$, $C_P = \tfrac{7}{2}R$.
At constant pressure: $\Delta Q = nC_P\Delta T$, $\Delta U = nC_V\Delta T$, $\Delta W = nR\Delta T$.
$\Delta Q:\Delta U:\Delta W = \tfrac{7}{2}:\tfrac{5}{2}:1 = 7:5:2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two charged conducting spheres $\mathrm{S_1}$ and $\mathrm{S_2}$ of radii 8 cm and 18 cm are connected to each other by a wire. After equilibrium is established, the ratio of electric fields on $\mathrm{S_1}$ and $\mathrm{S_2}$ spheres are $\mathrm{E_{S1}}$ and $\mathrm{E_{S2}}$ respectively. The value of $\dfrac{\mathrm{E_{S1}}}{\mathrm{E_{S2}}}$ is ________.
questions.sol:
Connected spheres reach the same potential: $\dfrac{kq_1}{r_1} = \dfrac{kq_2}{r_2} = V$.
Surface field $E = \dfrac{kq}{r^2} = \dfrac{V}{r}$, so $E \propto \dfrac{1}{r}$.
$\dfrac{E_{S1}}{E_{S2}} = \dfrac{r_2}{r_1} = \dfrac{18}{8} = \dfrac{9}{4}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The equation of a plane progressive wave is given by $y = 5\cos\pi\left(200\,t - \dfrac{x}{150}\right)$ where $x$ and $y$ are in cm and $t$ is in second. The velocity of the wave is ________ m/s.
questions.sol:
$\omega = 200\pi\ \mathrm{rad/s}$, $k = \dfrac{\pi}{150}\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}$.
$v = \dfrac{\omega}{k} = 200\times150 = 30000\ \mathrm{cm/s} = 300\ \mathrm{m/s}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two short electric dipoles $A$ and $B$ having dipole moment $\mathrm{p_1}$ and $\mathrm{p_2}$ respectively are placed with their axis mutually perpendicular as shown in the figure. The resultant electric field at a point $x$ is making an angle of $60^\circ$ with the line joining points O and $x$. The ratio of the dipole moments $\mathrm{p_2/p_1}$ is ________.
questions.sol:
Point $x$ (distance $r$ from O) lies on the axis of dipole A: $E_A = \dfrac{2kp_1}{r^3}$ along the line O$x$.
It lies on the equatorial line of dipole B: $E_B = \dfrac{kp_2}{r^3}$ perpendicular to O$x$.
$\tan60^\circ = \dfrac{E_B}{E_A} = \dfrac{p_2}{2p_1}$, so $\dfrac{p_2}{p_1} = 2\sqrt{3}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: For the given circuit (shown in part (A)) the time dependent input voltage $v_{in}(t)$ and corresponding output $v_o(t)$ are shown in part (B) and part (C), respectively. Identify the components that are used in the circuit between points X and Y.
questions.sol:
In the shunt branch, the ideal diode conducts from X to Y and the Zener ($V_Z = 5$ V) is reverse biased in that direction, so for the positive half cycle $v_o$ is clamped at $+5$ V.
In the negative half cycle that branch is open, yet the output is clamped at $-5$ V. So between X and Y there must be a path that conducts from Y to X with a 5 V drop.
That needs an ideal diode pointing towards X (conducting Y $\rightarrow$ X) in series with a Zener that is reverse biased for current Y $\rightarrow$ X, i.e. it breaks down at 5 V.
Only option (2) has this arrangement: a diode pointing towards X and a Zener whose forward direction is towards Y.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: When a coil is placed in a time dependent magnetic field the power dissipated in it is $P$. The number of turns, area of the coil and radius of the coil wire are $N$, $A$ and $r$ respectively. For a second coils number of turns, area of the coil and radius of the coil wire are $2N$, $2A$ and $3r$ respectively. When the first coil is replaced with second coil the power dissipated in it is $\sqrt{2}\,\alpha P$. The value of $\alpha$ is ______.
questions.sol:
Induced emf $\varepsilon = NA\dfrac{dB}{dt} \propto NA$.
Wire length $\ell \propto N\sqrt{A}$ (circumference $\propto\sqrt{A}$), so $R = \dfrac{\rho\ell}{\pi r^2} \propto \dfrac{N\sqrt{A}}{r^2}$.
$P = \dfrac{\varepsilon^2}{R} \propto N A^{3/2} r^2$.
$\dfrac{P'}{P} = 2\times(2)^{3/2}\times9 = 36\sqrt{2}$, so $\alpha = 36$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two identical long current carrying wires are bent into the shapes shown in the following figures. If the magnitude of magnetic fields at the centres P and Q of a semicircular arc are $\mathrm{B_1}$ and $\mathrm{B_2}$ respectively, then the ratio $\dfrac{\mathrm{B_1}}{\mathrm{B_2}}$ is ______.
questions.sol:
Semicircular arc at its centre: $\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4r}$. A semi-infinite wire ending at the foot of the perpendicular from the point: $\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}$. All contributions point the same way.
(I): two semi-infinite wires + arc: $B_1 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}(2+\pi)$.
(II): the horizontal semi-infinite wire + arc. The vertical wire is taken as lying along a line through Q, so it adds nothing: $B_2 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}(1+\pi)$.
$\dfrac{B_1}{B_2} = \dfrac{2+\pi}{1+\pi}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: For a thin symmetric prism made of glass (refractive index 1.5), the ratio of incident angle and minimum deviation will be ________.
questions.sol:
Thin prism: $\delta_m = (\mu-1)A = 0.5A$.
At minimum deviation $i = \dfrac{A+\delta_m}{2} = \dfrac{1.5A}{2} = 0.75A$.
$i:\delta_m = 0.75:0.5 = 3:2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Refer the figure given below. $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ are refractive indices of air and lens material. The height of image will be ________ cm.
questions.sol:
Single refracting surface: $\dfrac{\mu_2}{v} - \dfrac{\mu_1}{u} = \dfrac{\mu_2-\mu_1}{R}$ with $u = -40$ cm, $R = -20$ cm (centre C on the object side).
$\dfrac{1.54}{v} + \dfrac{1}{40} = \dfrac{0.54}{-20} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1.54}{v} = -0.052 \Rightarrow v \approx -29.6$ cm.
$m = \dfrac{\mu_1 v}{\mu_2 u} = \dfrac{-29.6}{1.54\times(-40)} \approx 0.48$.
Image height $\approx 0.48\times2 \approx 0.96 \approx 1$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: For a certain metal, when monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda$ is incident, the stopping potential for photoelectrons is $3V_o$. When the same metal is illuminated by light of wavelength $2\lambda$, then the stopping potential becomes $V_o$. The threshold wavelength for photoelectric emission for the given metal is $\alpha\lambda$. The value of $\alpha$ is ______.
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \phi = 3eV_o$ and $\dfrac{hc}{2\lambda} - \phi = eV_o$.
Subtracting: $\dfrac{hc}{2\lambda} = 2eV_o \Rightarrow eV_o = \dfrac{hc}{4\lambda}$.
$\phi = \dfrac{hc}{2\lambda} - \dfrac{hc}{4\lambda} = \dfrac{hc}{4\lambda}$, so $\lambda_0 = \dfrac{hc}{\phi} = 4\lambda$ and $\alpha = 4$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An electromagnetic wave travelling in $x$-direction is described by field equation $E_y = 300\sin\omega\left(t - \dfrac{x}{c}\right)$. If the electron is restricted to move in $y$-direction only with speed of $1.5\times10^6$ m/s then ratio of maximum electric and magnetic forces acting on the electron is ________.
questions.sol:
$B_0 = \dfrac{E_0}{c}$ (along $z$), perpendicular to the electron's velocity along $y$.
$\dfrac{F_E}{F_B} = \dfrac{eE_0}{evB_0} = \dfrac{c}{v} = \dfrac{3\times10^8}{1.5\times10^6} = 200$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Angular momentum of an electron in a hydrogen atom is $\dfrac{3h}{\pi}$, then the energy of the electron is ______ eV.
questions.sol:
Bohr: $L = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi} = \dfrac{3h}{\pi} \Rightarrow n = 6$.
$E_6 = -\dfrac{13.6}{36} \approx -0.38$ eV.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A liquid drop of diameter 2 mm breaks into 512 droplets. The change in surface energy is $\alpha\times10^{-6}$ J. The value of $\alpha$ is ________. (Take surface tension of liquid $= 0.08$ N/m)
questions.sol:
Volume conserved: $512r^3 = R^3 \Rightarrow r = R/8$, with $R = 1$ mm.
$\Delta A = 4\pi(512r^2 - R^2) = 4\pi R^2(8-1) = 28\pi\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm{m^2}$.
$\Delta E = T\Delta A = 0.08\times28\pi\times10^{-6} \approx 7.04\times10^{-6}$ J, so $\alpha \approx 7$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In single slit diffraction pattern, the wavelength of light used is 628 nm and slit width is 0.2 mm, the angular width of central maximum is $\alpha\times10^{-2}$ degrees. The value of $\alpha$ is ________.
questions.sol:
Angular width of central maximum $= \dfrac{2\lambda}{a} = \dfrac{2\times628\times10^{-9}}{0.2\times10^{-3}} = 6.28\times10^{-3}$ rad.
In degrees: $6.28\times10^{-3}\times\dfrac{180}{\pi} \approx 0.36^\circ = 36\times10^{-2}$ degrees, so $\alpha = 36$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A vessel contains $0.15\ \mathrm{m^3}$ of a gas at pressure 8 bar and temperature 140 °C with $c_p = 3R$ and $c_v = 2R$. It is expanded adiabatically till pressure falls to 1 bar. The work done during this process is ________ k J. (R is gas constant)
questions.sol:
$\gamma = \dfrac{c_p}{c_v} = 1.5$.
$V_2 = V_1\left(\dfrac{P_1}{P_2}\right)^{1/\gamma} = 0.15\times8^{2/3} = 0.6\ \mathrm{m^3}$.
$W = \dfrac{P_1V_1 - P_2V_2}{\gamma-1} = \dfrac{8\times10^5\times0.15 - 10^5\times0.6}{0.5} = \dfrac{0.6\times10^5}{0.5} = 1.2\times10^5$ J $= 120$ kJ.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: 1 $\mu$C charge moving with velocity $\vec{v} = \left(\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}\right)$ m/s in the region of magnetic field $\vec{B} = \left(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 5\hat{k}\right)$ T. The magnitude of force acting on it is $\sqrt{\alpha}\times10^{-6}$ N. The value of $\alpha$ is ________.
questions.sol:
$\vec{v}\times\vec{B} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & -5 \end{vmatrix} = (10-9)\hat{i} - (-5-6)\hat{j} + (3+4)\hat{k} = \hat{i} + 11\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}$.
$|\vec{v}\times\vec{B}| = \sqrt{1+121+49} = \sqrt{171}$.
$F = q|\vec{v}\times\vec{B}| = \sqrt{171}\times10^{-6}$ N, so $\alpha = 171$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A uniform wire of length $l$ of weight w is suspended from the roof with a weight of W at the other end. The stress in the wire at $\dfrac{l}{3}$ distance from the top is $\left(\dfrac{\mathrm{W}}{\mathrm{A}} + \dfrac{2}{\gamma}\dfrac{\mathrm{w}}{\mathrm{A}}\right)$, where, A is the cross sectional area of the wire. The value of $\gamma$ is ________.
questions.sol:
At distance $l/3$ from the top, the wire below has length $\tfrac{2l}{3}$ and weight $\tfrac{2}{3}w$.
Tension there $= W + \tfrac{2}{3}w$, so stress $= \dfrac{W}{A} + \dfrac{2}{3}\dfrac{w}{A}$.
Comparing, $\gamma = 3$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A tub is filled with water and a wooden cube 10 cm $\times$ 10 cm $\times$ 10 cm is placed in the water. The wooden cube is found to float on the water with a part of it submerged in water. When a metal coin is placed on the wooden cube, the submerged part is increased by 3.87 cm. The mass of the metal coin is ________ gram.
(Take water density as $1\ \mathrm{g/cm^3}$ and density of wood as $0.4\ \mathrm{g/cm^3}$)
questions.sol:
Without the coin, 4 cm is submerged ($0.4\times10$). With the coin, 7.87 cm is submerged, which is still less than 10 cm, so the cube still floats.
Extra buoyancy = weight of coin: $m = \rho_w A\,\Delta h = 1\times100\times3.87 = 387$ g.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The mass of iron converted into $\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}$ by the action of 18 g of steam is :
(Given : Molar mass of H, O and Fe are 1, 16 and 56 g mol$^{-1}$ respectively)
Assume iron is present in excess :
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{3Fe + 4H_2O \rightarrow Fe_3O_4 + 4H_2}$.
18 g steam = 1 mol $\mathrm{H_2O}$.
Fe reacted $= \tfrac{3}{4}$ mol $= 0.75 \times 56 = 42$ g.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
What is the energy (in J atom$^{-1}$) required for the following process ?
$\mathrm{Li^{2+}(g) \rightarrow Li^{3+}(g) + e^-}$
(Take the ionization energy for the H atom in the ground state as $2.18 \times 10^{-18}$ J atom$^{-1}$)
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Li^{2+}}$ is hydrogen-like with $Z = 3$, electron in $n = 1$.
$IE = Z^2 \times IE_\mathrm{H} = 9 \times 2.18 \times 10^{-18}$
$= 1.962 \times 10^{-17}$ J atom$^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : The correct sequence of bond lengths in the following species is :
$\mathrm{O_2^+ < O_2 < O_2^- < O_2^{2-}}$
Statement (II) : The correct sequence of number of unpaired electrons in the following species is :
$\mathrm{O_2 > O_2^+ > O_2^- > O_2^{2-}}$
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Bond orders (MOT): $\mathrm{O_2^+}$ 2.5, $\mathrm{O_2}$ 2, $\mathrm{O_2^-}$ 1.5, $\mathrm{O_2^{2-}}$ 1.
Bond length increases as bond order decreases, so Statement I is true.
Unpaired electrons: $\mathrm{O_2}$ 2, $\mathrm{O_2^+}$ 1, $\mathrm{O_2^-}$ 1, $\mathrm{O_2^{2-}}$ 0.
Since $\mathrm{O_2^+}$ and $\mathrm{O_2^-}$ both have 1, the order $\mathrm{O_2^+ > O_2^-}$ is wrong, so Statement II is false.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following data.
(i) $\mathrm{2Al(s) + 6HCl(aq) \rightarrow Al_2Cl_6(aq) + 3H_2(g) + 1200\ kJ/mol}$
(ii) $\mathrm{H_2(g) + Cl_2(g) \rightarrow 2HCl(g) + 164\ kJ/mol.}$
(iii) $\mathrm{HCl(g) + aq \rightarrow HCl(aq) + 83\ kJ/mol.}$
(iv) $\mathrm{Al_2Cl_6(s) + aq \rightarrow Al_2Cl_6(aq) + 663\ kJ/mol}$
The enthalpy of formation of anhydrous solid $\mathrm{Al_2Cl_6}$ is :
questions.sol:
Target: $\mathrm{2Al(s) + 3Cl_2(g) \rightarrow Al_2Cl_6(s)}$.
Heat released means $\Delta H$ negative: (i) $-1200$, (ii) $-164$, (iii) $-83$, (iv) $-663$ kJ.
Target = (i) + 3(ii) + 6(iii) $-$ (iv).
$\Delta_f H = -1200 - 492 - 498 + 663 = -1527$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: 19.5 g of fluoro acetic acid (molar mass $=$ 78 g mol$^{-1}$) is dissolved in 500 g of water at 298 K. The depression in the freezing point of water was 1°C. What is $\mathrm{K_a}$ of fluoro acetic acid ? (For water, $\mathrm{K_f = 1.86\ K\ kg\ mol^{-1}}$). Assume molarity and molality to have same values.
questions.sol:
$m = \dfrac{19.5/78}{0.5} = 0.5$ mol kg$^{-1}$.
$\Delta T_f = i K_f m \Rightarrow i = \dfrac{1}{1.86 \times 0.5} = 1.075$, so $\alpha = i - 1 = 0.075$.
$K_a = \dfrac{C\alpha^2}{1-\alpha} = \dfrac{0.5 \times (0.075)^2}{0.925} \approx 3 \times 10^{-3}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The solubility product constants of $\mathrm{Ag_2CrO_4}$ and AgBr are $32x$ and $4y$ respectively at 298 K.
The value of $\left(\dfrac{\text{molarity of } \mathrm{Ag_2CrO_4}}{\text{molarity of AgBr}}\right)$ can be expressed as :
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Ag_2CrO_4}$: $K_{sp} = 4s_1^3 = 32x \Rightarrow s_1 = 2\sqrt[3]{x}$.
AgBr: $K_{sp} = s_2^2 = 4y \Rightarrow s_2 = 2\sqrt{y}$.
$\dfrac{s_1}{s_2} = \dfrac{\sqrt[3]{x}}{\sqrt{y}}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
An electrochemical cell is constructed using half cells in the direction of spontaneous change
$\mathrm{Fe(OH)_2(s) + 2e^- \rightarrow Fe(s) + 2OH^-(aq)} \qquad \mathrm{E^{\theta} = -0.88\ V}$
and $\mathrm{AgBr(s) + e^- \rightarrow Ag(s) + Br^-(aq)} \qquad \mathrm{E^{\theta} = +0.07\ V}$
Which of the following option is correct ?
options: Fe is reduced in the electrochemical cell
questions.sol:
Higher reduction potential (AgBr/Ag, $+0.07$ V) is the cathode; Fe/Fe(OH)$_2$ is the anode (Fe is oxidised).
Overall: $\mathrm{Fe + 2OH^- + 2AgBr \rightleftharpoons Fe(OH)_2 + 2Ag + 2Br^-}$.
$E^\theta_{cell} = 0.07 - (-0.88) = +0.95$ V, and $E^\theta_{cell}$ is intensive.
Only the first option is correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: $\mathrm{t_{100\%}}$ is the time required for the 100% completion of the reaction while $\mathrm{t_{1/2}}$ is the time required for 50% of the reaction to be completed. Which of the following option correctly represents the relation between $\mathrm{t_{100\%}}$ and $\mathrm{t_{1/2}}$ for zero and first order reactions respectively ?
questions.sol:
Zero order: $[A] = [A]_0 - kt$, so $t_{100\%} = [A]_0/k$ and $t_{1/2} = [A]_0/2k$, giving $t_{100\%} = 2t_{1/2}$.
First order: $t = \dfrac{1}{k}\ln\dfrac{[A]_0}{[A]}$ diverges as $[A] \to 0$, so 100% completion takes infinite time, written $(t_{1/2})^{\infty}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : The first ionisation enthalpy of the elements Na, Mg, Cl and Ar follows the order Na > Mg > Cl > Ar.
Statement (II) : Among Ca, Al, Fe and B, the third ionisation enthalpy is very high for Ca.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Across period 3 the first ionisation enthalpy increases: Ar > Cl > Mg > Na, so Statement I is false.
$\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$ has a noble-gas (Ar) configuration, so removing a third electron needs very high energy; Al, B and Fe lose a third electron relatively easily. Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : Oxidising power of halogens decreases in the order $\mathrm{F_2 > Cl_2 > Br_2 > I_2}$, which is the basis of “Layer test”.
Statement (II) : “Layer test” to identify $\mathrm{Br_2}$ and $\mathrm{I_2}$ in aqueous solution involves the oxidation of bromide or iodide into $\mathrm{Br_2}$ or $\mathrm{I_2}$ respectively with $\mathrm{Cl_2}$, which is a type of displacement redox reaction.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Oxidising power: $\mathrm{F_2 > Cl_2 > Br_2 > I_2}$, so a halogen displaces the halide ions below it.
In the layer test $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ water oxidises $\mathrm{Br^-}$/$\mathrm{I^-}$ to $\mathrm{Br_2}$/$\mathrm{I_2}$, which colour the organic layer (orange/violet) — a displacement redox reaction.
Both statements are true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which of the following sets includes all the species that will change the orange colour of $\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}$ in acidic medium ?
questions.sol:
Acidified dichromate (orange) turns green ($\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$) only with reducing agents.
$\mathrm{Fe^{2+}, Sn^{2+}, I^-, S^{2-}}$ are all reducing.
$\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$, $\mathrm{Sn^{4+}}$ and $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$ are in their higher oxidation states and cannot reduce it, so every other set contains a non-reacting species.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - I
Chromium (III) Complexes
(en = ethylene diamine)		List - II
$\Delta_0(\mathrm{cm^{-1}})$
A. $\mathrm{[Cr(CN)_6]^{3-}}$I. 15,060
B. $\mathrm{[CrF_6]^{3-}}$II. 17,400
C. $\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}$III. 22,300
D. $\mathrm{[Cr(en)_3]^{3+}}$IV. 26,600
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Spectrochemical series: $\mathrm{F^- < H_2O < en < CN^-}$.
So $\Delta_0$: $\mathrm{[CrF_6]^{3-}}$ smallest (15,060), $\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}$ 17,400, $\mathrm{[Cr(en)_3]^{3+}}$ 22,300, $\mathrm{[Cr(CN)_6]^{3-}}$ largest (26,600).
A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : 1,2,3-Trihydroxypropane can be separated from water by simple distillation.
Statement (II) : An azeotropic mixture cannot be separated by fractional distillation.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
1,2,3-Trihydroxypropane (glycerol) decomposes at/below its normal boiling point (~563 K), so it is separated/purified by distillation under reduced pressure, not by simple distillation: Statement I is false.
An azeotrope boils at constant temperature with vapour of the same composition as the liquid, so fractional distillation cannot separate it: Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : Benzyl chloride reacts faster in $\mathrm{S_N1}$ mechanism than ethyl chloride.
Statement (II) : Ethyl carbocation intermediate is less stabilized by hyperconjugation than benzyl carbocation by resonance.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{S_N1}$ rate depends on carbocation stability.
The benzyl cation is delocalised over the ring by resonance, far more stable than the ethyl cation (only hyperconjugation).
So benzyl chloride reacts faster; both statements are true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: In IUPAC nomenclature, the correct order of decreasing priority of functional group is :
questions.sol:
IUPAC seniority: acid > ester > acid halide > amide > nitrile > aldehyde > ketone > alcohol > amine > alkene/alkyne.
So $\mathrm{-CONH_2 > -CHO > \ >C=O > -NH_2 > -C\equiv C-}$.
(Ester ranks above amide and $\mathrm{-OH}$ above $\mathrm{-NH_2}$; nitrile ranks above aldehyde — so the other options are wrong.)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: For the given molecule, “$x$”, the preferred site for the attack of the electrophile is :
questions.sol:
$x$ is benzanilide, $\mathrm{C_6H_5CO{-}NH{-}C_6H_5}$.
The ring on N carries $\mathrm{-NHCOR}$: the N lone pair activates it and directs ortho/para.
The ring on C=O carries $\mathrm{-CONHR}$, which is deactivating (meta-directing), so it is not attacked.
On the activated ring the bulky amide group hinders the ortho position (s), so attack is predominantly para, at “u”.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - I
Mixture of Compounds		List - II
Reagent used to distinguish
A. Diethyl amine + Ethyl amineI. Bromine water
B. Acetaldehyde + AcetoneII. $\mathrm{CHCl_3 + KOH, \Delta}$
C. Ethanol + PhenolIII. Neutral $\mathrm{FeCl_3}$
D. Benzoic acid + Cinnamic acidIV. Ammonical silver nitrate
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A: carbylamine test ($\mathrm{CHCl_3}$ + KOH, $\Delta$) — only the primary amine (ethyl amine) gives the foul-smelling isocyanide → II.
B: Tollens' reagent (ammonical $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$) — only acetaldehyde gives a silver mirror → IV.
C: neutral $\mathrm{FeCl_3}$ — phenol gives violet colour → III.
D: bromine water — cinnamic acid (C=C) decolourises it → I.
A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the three aromatic molecules (P, Q and R) whose structures have been given below :
The correct order regarding the reactivity of these compounds with $\mathrm{Ph-\underset{(+)}{N}\equiv N\,Cl^{(-)}}$ under optimum but slightly acidic medium is :
questions.sol:
Diazo coupling is electrophilic substitution at the para position, which needs the $\mathrm{NMe_2}$ lone pair in resonance with the ring.
Ortho-methyl groups force the $\mathrm{NMe_2}$ group out of the ring plane (steric inhibition of resonance), reducing activation.
P (no ortho Me) is most activated, Q (one ortho Me) less, R (two ortho Me) least.
Order: P > Q > R.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - I
Vitamin		List - II
Name
A. Vitamin $\mathrm{B_1}$I. Pyridoxine
B. Vitamin $\mathrm{B_2}$II. Ascorbic acid
C. Vitamin $\mathrm{B_6}$III. Thiamine
D. Vitamin CIV. Riboflavin
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{B_1}$ = thiamine (III), $\mathrm{B_2}$ = riboflavin (IV), $\mathrm{B_6}$ = pyridoxine (I), vitamin C = ascorbic acid (II).
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: A salt with few drops of conc. HCl gives apple green colour in flame test. The group precipitate of the salt is dissolved in acetic acid and treated with $\mathrm{K_2CrO_4}$ to give yellow precipitate. When the sodium carbonate extract of the salt solution is heated with conc. $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ and ammonium molybdate, it resulted a canary yellow precipitate. The cation and anion present in the salt are respectively,
questions.sol:
Apple green flame and yellow $\mathrm{BaCrO_4}$ with $\mathrm{K_2CrO_4}$ in acetic acid → $\mathrm{Ba^{2+}}$.
Canary yellow precipitate with ammonium molybdate/conc. $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ (ammonium phosphomolybdate) → $\mathrm{PO_4^{3-}}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
5.33 g of $\mathrm{CrCl_3\cdot 6H_2O}$, which is a 1 : 3 electrolyte, is dissolved in water and is passed through a cation exchanger. The chloride ions in the eluted solution, on treatment with $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$ results in 8.61 g of AgCl. The ratio of moles of complex reacted and moles of AgCl formed is ________ $\times 10^{-2}$. (Nearest integer)
[Molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ Cr : 52, Ag : 108, Cl : 35.5, H : 1, O : 16]
questions.sol:
Molar mass of $\mathrm{CrCl_3\cdot 6H_2O} = 52 + 106.5 + 108 = 266.5$; moles $= 5.33/266.5 = 0.02$.
Moles AgCl $= 8.61/143.5 = 0.06$ (all three Cl ionisable: $\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_6]Cl_3}$, 1 : 3 electrolyte).
Ratio $= 0.02/0.06 = 0.333 = 33 \times 10^{-2}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Consider the isomers of hydrocarbon with molecular formula $\mathrm{C_5H_{10}}$. These isomers do not decolourise $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ solution. These isomers are subjected to chlorination with chlorine in presence of light to give monochloro compounds. The total number of monochloro compounds (structural isomers only) formed is ________.
questions.sol:
Not decolourising $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ → cycloalkanes $\mathrm{C_5H_{10}}$.
Cyclopentane: 1; methylcyclobutane: 4 ($\mathrm{CH_2Cl}$, C1, C2, C3); ethylcyclopropane: 4 ($\mathrm{CH_3}$, $\mathrm{CH_2}$, C1, ring $\mathrm{CH_2}$); 1,1-dimethylcyclopropane: 2 ($\mathrm{CH_3}$, ring $\mathrm{CH_2}$); 1,2-dimethylcyclopropane: 3 ($\mathrm{CH_3}$, C1, C3).
Total $= 1 + 4 + 4 + 2 + 3 = 14$.

questions.text: One mole of an alkane (x) requires 8 mole oxygen for complete combustion. Sum of number of carbon and hydrogen atoms in the alkane (x) is ________.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2} + \dfrac{3n+1}{2}O_2 \rightarrow nCO_2 + (n+1)H_2O}$.
$\dfrac{3n+1}{2} = 8 \Rightarrow n = 5$, alkane $\mathrm{C_5H_{12}}$.
$5 + 12 = 17$.

questions.text:
For reaction $\mathrm{A \rightarrow P}$, rate constant $\mathrm{k = 1.5 \times 10^3\ s^{-1}}$ at 27°C
If activation energy for the above reaction is 60 kJ mol$^{-1}$, then the temperature (in °C) at which rate constant, $\mathrm{k = 4.5 \times 10^3\ s^{-1}}$ is ________. (Nearest integer)
Given : log 2 $=$ 0.30, log 3 $=$ 0.48, R $=$ 8.3 J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$, ln 10 $=$ 2.3
questions.sol:
$\ln\dfrac{k_2}{k_1} = \dfrac{E_a}{R}\left(\dfrac{1}{T_1} - \dfrac{1}{T_2}\right)$, with $k_2/k_1 = 3$, $\ln 3 = 2.3 \times 0.48 = 1.104$.
$\dfrac{E_a}{R} = \dfrac{60000}{8.3} = 7229$ K.
$\dfrac{1}{T_2} = \dfrac{1}{300} - \dfrac{1.104}{7229} = 0.0031806 \Rightarrow T_2 \approx 314.4$ K.
$t \approx 41$°C.

questions.text: At the transition temperature T, $\mathrm{A \rightleftharpoons B}$ and $\Delta G^0 = 105 - 35\log T$ where A and B are two states of substance X. The transition temperature in °C when pressure is 1 atm is ________. (Nearest integer)
questions.sol:
At the transition temperature (1 atm) the two states are in equilibrium under standard conditions, so $\Delta G^0 = 0$.
$105 = 35\log T \Rightarrow \log T = 3 \Rightarrow T = 1000$ K.
$t = 1000 - 273 = 727$°C.
